label: Chapter 20
title: The Land of Beulah and the River

blocks.p: Now I saw in my dream that by this time the pilgrims had crossed the Enchanted Ground and were entering the country of Beulah, whose air was very sweet and pleasant; and since the road ran straight through it, they rested and refreshed themselves there for a while. Here they heard the birds singing all the time, and saw the flowers appear on the earth every day, and heard the cooing of the turtledove in the land. [Isa. 62:4; Song of Solomon 2:10-12] In this country the sun shines night and day; for it lay beyond the Valley of the Shadow of Death, and out of the reach of Giant Despair; and from here they could not so much as see Doubting Castle. Here they were within sight of the city they were going to; and here some of its inhabitants came to meet them, for the Shining Ones commonly walked in this land, because it lay on the borders of heaven. In this land, too, the marriage contract between the bride and the bridegroom was renewed; yes, here, “as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so their God rejoiced over them.” [Isa. 62:5] Here they had no lack of grain and wine; for in this place they found plenty of everything they had sought for in all their pilgrimage. [Isa. 62:8] Here they heard voices from the city, loud voices, saying, “Say to the daughter of Zion, ‘Look, your salvation is coming! Look, his reward is with him!’” And here all the people of the country called them “The holy people, The redeemed of the Lord, Sought out,” and so on. [Isa. 62:11-12]

Now as they walked in this land, they rejoiced more than they had in places farther from the kingdom they were bound for; and as they drew near to the city, they had a still clearer view of it. It was built of pearls and precious stones, and its street was paved with gold; so that, with the natural glory of the city and the sunlight shining back from it, Christian fell sick with longing; and Hopeful also had a bout or two of the same sickness. So they lay there for a while, crying out because of their pangs, “If you find my beloved, tell him that I am sick with love.”

But when they had grown a little stronger, and were better able to bear their sickness, they walked on their way and came nearer and nearer, where there were orchards, vineyards, and gardens whose gates opened onto the highway. As they came up to these places, they saw the gardener standing in the road, and the pilgrims said to him, “Whose fine vineyards and gardens are these?”

“They are the King’s,” he answered, “and they are planted here for his own delight, and also for the comfort of pilgrims.” So the gardener took them into the vineyards and told them to refresh themselves with the delicacies there. [Deut. 23:24] He also showed them the King’s walks, and the arbors where he loved to be; and here they stayed and slept.

Now I saw in my dream that they talked more in their sleep at this time than they had in all their journey; and as I was wondering about it, the gardener said to me, “Why are you puzzling over this? It is the nature of the grapes of these vineyards to go down so sweetly that they make the lips of those who are asleep to speak.”

So I saw that when they woke, they set out to go up to the city. But, as I said, the sunlight shining back from the city, for the city was pure gold, was so extremely glorious that they could not yet look at it with unveiled face, but only through an instrument made for that purpose. So I saw that as they went on, two men met them, in clothing that shone like gold; and their faces shone like the light. [Rev. 21:18; 2 Cor. 3:18]

These men asked the pilgrims where they had come from, and they told them. They also asked them where they had lodged, and what difficulties and dangers, what comforts and pleasures, they had met on the way; and they told them.
“You have only two more difficulties to meet,” said the men, “and then you are in the city.”
Then Christian and his companion asked the men to go along with them, and they said they would. “But,” they said, “you must get there by your own faith.”
So I saw in my dream that they went on together until they came in sight of the gate.

Now I further saw that between them and the gate was a river, and there was no bridge to cross it; and the river was very deep. At the sight of this river the pilgrims were stunned; but the men who went with them said, “You must go through, or you cannot reach the gate.”

The pilgrims then began to ask whether there was any other way to the gate. “Yes,” they answered, “but no one except two, Enoch and Elijah, has been allowed to walk that path since the foundation of the world, nor will anyone be, until the last trumpet sounds.” [1 Cor. 15:51-52]
(That is, in the resurrection of the righteous. [Rev. 20:4-6])

Then the pilgrims, and especially Christian, began to lose heart, and looked this way and that; but they could find no way to escape the river. Then they asked the men whether the waters were all the same depth.
“No,” they said; but they could not help them there. “You will find it deeper or shallower,” they said, “according to how you believe in the King of the place.”

So they set out into the water; and as they went in, Christian began to sink, and he cried out to his good friend Hopeful, “I am sinking in deep waters; the waves are going over my head; all his breakers are going over me! Selah.”
Then Hopeful said, “Take heart, my brother. I can feel the bottom, and it is good.”

“Ah, my friend,” said Christian, “the sorrows of death have surrounded me. I will not see the land that flows with milk and honey.” And with that a great darkness and horror fell on Christian, so that he could not see ahead of him. Here, too, he largely lost his senses, so that he could neither remember nor speak in any orderly way of any of the sweet refreshments he had met with on his pilgrimage. Everything he said showed that he was in horror of mind, and afraid in his heart that he would die in that river and never be let in at the gate. Here also, as those who stood by could see, he was deeply troubled by thoughts of the sins he had committed, both before and after he became a pilgrim. It was also noticed that he was troubled by apparitions of hobgoblins and evil spirits, for every now and then his words gave it away.

So Hopeful had a hard time keeping his brother’s head above water. Sometimes Christian would go under completely, and then after a while he would come up again, half dead. Hopeful would also try to comfort him, saying, “Brother, I see the gate, and men standing by it to receive us.”
But Christian would answer, “It’s you, it’s you they’re waiting for. You have been Hopeful ever since I’ve known you.”
“And so have you,” said Hopeful to Christian.
“Ah, brother,” he said, “surely, if I were right with him, he would come now to help me. But for my sins he has brought me into the snare and left me.”

“My brother,” said Hopeful, “you have quite forgotten the text where it is said of the wicked, ‘They have no struggles in their death; their strength is firm. They are not in trouble as other men are, nor are they plagued like other men.’ [Ps. 73:4-5] These troubles and distresses you are going through in these waters are no sign that God has abandoned you. They are sent to test you: to see whether you will call to mind what you have already received of his goodness, and lean on him in your distress.”
Then I saw in my dream that Christian seemed lost in thought for a while. And Hopeful added this word: “Take heart. Jesus Christ makes you whole.”

And with that Christian broke out with a loud voice, “Oh, I see him again! And he tells me, ‘When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you.’” [Isa. 43:2]

Then they both took courage, and after that the enemy was as still as a stone until they had crossed over. Christian soon found ground to stand on, and from there on the rest of the river was shallow. So they got over.

Now on the bank of the river, on the other side, they saw the two shining men again, waiting there for them. When they had come up out of the river, the men greeted them, saying, “We are ministering spirits, sent out to serve those who will inherit salvation.” And so they went along toward the gate.

Now you must understand that the city stood on a mighty hill; but the pilgrims went up that hill with ease, because they had these two men to lead them up by the arms. Besides, they had left their mortal garments behind them in the river; for though they went in with them, they came out without them. So they went up here with great speed and lightness, though the foundation the city was built on was higher than the clouds. They went up through the regions of the air, talking sweetly as they went, comforted because they had safely crossed the river and had such glorious companions to attend them.

v: Look now, look how the holy pilgrims ride!
The clouds their chariots, angels for their guide.
Who would not risk it all for such a One,
who so provides for his when this world’s done?

blocks.p: Their talk with the Shining Ones was about the glory of the place; and the Shining Ones told them that its beauty and glory were beyond words.

“There,” they said, “is Mount Zion, the heavenly Jerusalem, the innumerable company of angels, and the spirits of righteous men made perfect. [Heb. 12:22-24] You are going now to the paradise of God, where you will see the tree of life, and eat of its never-fading fruit; and when you come there, you will be given white robes, and every day you will walk and talk with the King, for all the days of eternity. [Rev. 2:7; 3:4; 21:4-5] There you will never again see what you saw in the lower region, on the earth: sorrow, sickness, affliction, and death; for the former things have passed away. You are going now to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, and to the prophets, men whom God has taken away from the evil to come, and who are now resting on their beds, each one walking in his righteousness.” [Isa. 57:1-2; 65:17]
“What must we do in the holy place?” the men asked.

“There you will receive the comfort of all your toil, and have joy for all your sorrow. You will reap what you have sown, the fruit of all your prayers and tears and sufferings for the King along the way. [Gal. 6:7] In that place you will wear crowns of gold, and enjoy the unending sight and vision of the Holy One, for there you will see him as he is. [1 John 3:2] There, too, you will serve him continually with praise, with shouting and thanksgiving, the One you longed to serve in the world, though with great difficulty, because of the weakness of your flesh. There your eyes will be delighted with seeing, and your ears with hearing the pleasant voice of the Mighty One. There you will enjoy again your friends who have gone there before you; and there you will joyfully welcome every one who follows you into the holy place. There, too, you will be clothed with glory and majesty, and fitted out to ride with the King of Glory. When he comes with the sound of the trumpet in the clouds, as on the wings of the wind, you will come with him; and when he sits on the throne of judgment, you will sit beside him; yes, and when he passes sentence on all who do evil, whether angels or men, you also will have a voice in that judgment, because they were his enemies and yours. [1 Thess. 4:13-16; Jude 1:14; Dan. 7:9-10; 1 Cor. 6:2-3] And when he returns to the city again, you will go too, with the sound of the trumpet, and be with him forever.”
